delimiters, leaving one classic blob. kses_remove_filters(); wp_insert_post( array( 'import_id' => 9999, 'post_type' => 'post', 'post_status' => 'draft', 'post_title' => 'Reading the block editor store: select() vs useSelect()', 'post_content' => <<<'HTML'

The notice at the top reads one number — the block count — from one store, core/block-editor, four different ways. Three go through the wp.data global, one uses the useSelect hook. Only some of them are telling you the truth.

Try it

  • Add or delete a block. The useSelect column and row C move immediately.
  • Rows A and B don’t move at all — they get flagged STALE.
  • Reload. Row A drops to 0 and stays there.

What each row is doing

  • A · read at load — select() runs once before the editor hydrates, reads 0, and never runs again.
  • B · read on demand — select() was correct the moment it ran, but it never re-reads itself. You can ask again by hand, on every click — but that’s you doing the work.
  • C · subscribe() — right number, always. You wrote the subscription, the diffing, and the cleanup.
  • useSelect() — right number, always. It starts empty too, then re-renders itself once the store hydrates and on every change after. One line.

None of this is about reaching the store — the wp.data global reads the same store the editor uses, and row C proves it by ticking in step with the hook. The difference is when you read, and whether anything tells you it changed. select() is a snapshot; useSelect() is a subscription. Hit Show the code to see all four.
